items.title: Injectivity of the canonical map to the pushforward of a flat pullback when the relative associated points lie in the image
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for the canonical map from a flat finite type module to the pushforward of its pullback along a flat morphism to be injective, namely that the relative associated points of the module lie in the image of the morphism, and shows this property is stable under base change (statement lines 6597-6609, tag 05PD). The proof reduces base change stability to the same statement over the base, replaces injectivity by the vanishing of the weakly associated points of the kernel, uses that for a flat finite type module those points are relative associated ones, and then kills the kernel at each such point by faithful flatness of the induced local ring map. The chain of reductions through weakly associated points is the substance, so the claim is H2.
